groups.statement: The system shall make it easy for people who are new to online commerce to get a store up and running without requiring a lot of technical help.
The system shall allow store owners and sales staff to add and maintain products.
The system shall allow store owners and sales staff to manage customer accounts.
The system shall allow store owners and sales staff to process orders confidently through a simple interface.
The system shall reduce support requests.
Staff shall only be able to create or edit products that are active in the catalog.
The store shall not allow selling more items than are currently in stock unless backorders are later supported.
Customer accounts shall be validated to prevent duplicate or incomplete records.
The store shall prevent checkout when required customer details or shipping details are missing.
An order shall only be placed when the cart is confirmed and the items are still available.
If an order has already been processed, changes to the order shall be restricted and may require a staff override or cancellation workflow.
Sensitive actions such as deleting records shall have tighter restrictions for staff.
The store shall support clear pricing at checkout.
Prices should be shown before tax unless the customer’s region expects tax-inclusive display.
Tax should be calculated based on location rather than the product alone.
The store shall support discounts or promotions later.
Rounding should be handled consistently at checkout so the customer sees the final total clearly.
The system shall support card payments as the standard checkout payment option.
The system should include PayPal if it is practical to do so.
The system should not rely on cash on delivery as the default payment method.
The system may allow cash on delivery for special cases.
The system could support bank transfer for some customers.
The system shall keep payment options simple at launch rather than supporting all payment methods at once.
The system shall require the customer's name as a core address field.
The system shall require the street address as a core address field.
The system shall require the city as a core address field.
The system shall require the postal code as a core address field.
The system shall require the country as a core address field.
The system shall require a contact phone number or email address so shipping problems can be resolved.
The system shall validate the address format as much as possible based on the selected country or region.
The system shall be forgiving of international addresses and shall not force one rigid address format.
The system shall support manual exception handling for edge cases such as rural deliveries or businesses with special delivery instructions.
The system shall support the order statuses new, paid, packed, shipped, completed, and cancelled.
Customers shall be able to cancel an order only before shipping.
The system should support customers requesting a return after delivery.
The system shall provide low-stock warnings.
The low-stock threshold shall be configurable.
The low-stock threshold should be configurable per product.
The low-stock threshold should be configurable by category for some items.
Fast-moving products shall trigger earlier alerts than slow-selling products.
Low-stock warnings shall be sent to store owners.
Low-stock warnings shall be sent to staff responsible for purchasing or inventory.
Low-stock warnings shall enable restocking before inventory runs out.
At launch, the store shall support a standard delivery option.
At launch, the store shall support an express delivery option if the system can support it.
At checkout, the system shall show customers the available shipping methods based on their destination.
The system shall calculate shipping cost from basic rules such as region and possibly weight or order total.
If an address cannot be served by a shipping method, the system shall hide that option instead of allowing the customer to select it.
Customer registration shall be self-service with immediate access.
The system shall be able to place an account on hold if something looks suspicious or if verification fails.
The system shall support a pending status for held accounts.
The system shall support a blocked status for held accounts.
At launch, the store owner shall be able to configure the basic store settings during initial setup.
During initial setup, the store owner shall be able to configure the store name.
During initial setup, the store owner shall be able to configure contact details.
During initial setup, the store owner shall be able to configure the currency.
During initial setup, the store owner shall be able to configure tax settings.
During initial setup, the store owner shall be able to configure shipping methods.
During initial setup, the store owner shall be able to configure payment options.
The store shall not go live until the core settings are complete.
The storefront shall require certain fields to be completed when needed for checkout and invoices, including business address or legal details.
